items.prompt: Assess how far the role of the federal government changed between 1830 and 1910.
items.original_prompt: Evaluate the extent to which the role of the federal government changed from the period 1830 to 1910.

exemplar.thesis: The federal government's role changed enormously from 1830 to 1910: Jacksonian limited government gave way to Civil War-era activism and Gilded Age economic regulation, even as laissez-faire ideology and states' rights limited how far the change went.
evidence: Jacksonian era: veto of the Bank, limited federal role; Civil War expansion - Homestead Act, Morrill Act, Pacific Railway Act, and greenbacks
Gilded Age regulation: Interstate Commerce Act (1887), Sherman Antitrust Act (1890), and Progressive-era activism
Continuity: laissez-faire ideology persisted, the Supreme Court struck down labor regulation (e.g., Lochner era), and segregation showed federal unwillingness to protect civil rights
